summary: At step 20, JavaScript stops in doeat()’s resumed-meal branch before reaching fpostfx(); C continues into the cursed-apple post-effect and puts the hero to sleep. The immediate source owner is the whole doeat() function, with fpostfx() as a downstream gap shared with the royal-jelly case.

source.branch: When the selected FOOD_CLASS object is svc.context.victual.piece, doeat() treats it as a resumed meal. In this recording an earlier cursed-apple attempt ran rottenfood() and set dont_start; the retry has one bite left, so C prints “You consume the last bite of your meal.” and calls start_eating(). That function counts its bite, then calls done_eating(), whose non-corpse path calls fpostfx(). fpostfx() applies its APPLE arm when the object is cursed and the hero lacks Sleep_resistance; after its race, deafness, and acoustics message branch it calls fall_asleep(-rn1(11, 20), TRUE).
callers: C nethack-c/upstream/src/cmd.c:1712-1713 maps key e to doeat(); cmd.c:4803-4805 also enqueues doeat() for MCMD_EAT. JavaScript js/cmd.js:3223-3229 calls doeat() from runEatCommand(), and js/cmd.js:5102-5103 dispatches the command to that wrapper.
dependencies: C eat.c:1813-1851 rottenfood() participates in the prior cursed-food attempt; eat.c:3026-3036 sets dont_start and consumes oeaten after that result. This setup path is already implemented in js/eat.js and is not the current first stop.

C eat.c:2022-2074 start_eating() calls bite() and, when the bite reaches reqtime, calls done_eating(). JavaScript js/eat.js:3366-3435 provides these resumed-meal operations after doeat() returns from its matching-piece branch.

C eat.c:544-573 done_eating() calls fpostfx() for non-corpse food at lines 562-565. The cursed-APPLE behavior is in eat.c:2582-2597. JavaScript js/eat.js:3032-3216 still throws for that APPLE branch; fpostfx() is one whole static C function, and its royal-jelly branch is assigned to the other investigator. Coordinate that shared whole-function scope through the orchestrator.

evidence: The saved evaluation challenges/evaluations/20261003003219-v20.json is for commit b5bb23ff11504c300f032b10b1e17c99b06fc97e and reports 20/31 screens and cursors matched, 2743/2761 RNG calls matched, and a stop at zero-based step 20: “eating requires doeat()’s resumed meal.” The selected cache entry .cache/v20-work-queue.json records the same first mismatch and 11 remaining screens.

The C recording challenges/cases/v20/cursed-apple-fpostfx-after-rottenfood-v20.session.json has key o at step 20. Its response is “You consume the last bite of your meal.”; its RNG log begins rn2(11)=10 @ fpostfx(eat.c:2595), and its screen then says “You fall asleep.” The immutable prior C63 packet records the independent C replay of this same route.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/eat.c:2923-2950 owns the same-piece resumed-meal path and calls start_eating(); eat.c:2022-2074 reaches done_eating() when the one-bite meal completes; eat.c:544-573 calls fpostfx() for the non-corpse apple. The current JavaScript counterpart js/eat.js:4213-4217 throws before start_eating(), so doeat() is the actual first mismatch owner at this commit.

The required source scope is the complete eat.c:doeat() function (2817-3084), including existing partial branches, with its current command callers. After that earlier refusal is removed, this recording also exercises the APPLE branch of the complete eat.c:fpostfx() function (2510-2600). Keep fpostfx() with the shared royal-jelly whole-function task; this finding does not claim that the current first mismatch is already inside fpostfx().
